```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Chen 2016 fits two **separate** population PK models, one for lopinavir (LPV)
and one for ritonavir (RTV), each describing the total and the unbound
(protein-free) plasma concentration simultaneously in HIV-infected women
followed through pregnancy and postpartum. The authors also tested joint
LPV-RTV interaction models, found that none improved the fit significantly,
and did not adopt them, so only the two individual final models are packaged.

```{r models}
mod_names <- c(
  lopinavir = "Chen_2016_lopinavir",
  ritonavir = "Chen_2016_ritonavir"
)
uis <- lapply(mod_names, function(n) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(n)))
```

* Citation: `r uis$lopinavir$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12065>
* Supplementary Material S5 holds the authors' NONMEM control streams for both
  individual models and for the three interaction models, available from the
  [Europe PMC supplementary files for PMC4807435](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC4807435).

# Population

Twelve HIV-infected pregnant women taking lopinavir/ritonavir tablets with a
nucleoside backbone were enrolled at the University of North Carolina at Chapel
Hill and Northwestern University (NCT00766818). Each had intensive PK sampling
at four visits: 20-24 weeks of gestation on 400/100 mg twice daily; 30 weeks on
400/100 mg, after which the dose was increased to 500/125 mg twice daily; 32
weeks on 500/125 mg; and about 8 weeks postpartum back on 400/100 mg. Age was
18-35 years (median 28), screening weight 45.3-142.6 kg (median 87.4), 75% were
African American and 67% were antiretroviral-naive. Albumin and alpha-1 acid
glycoprotein were both significantly lower in pregnancy than postpartum. In
total 330 plasma samples were assayed for both total and unbound drug.

```{r population}
str(uis$lopinavir$population[c("n_subjects", "age_range", "weight_median", "race_ethnicity", "ga_range")])
```

# Model structure

Both drugs use the same structure (Figure 1). The central ODE state holds
*unbound* drug, so `cl` and `vc` are the apparent unbound parameters CLu/F
(the apparent intrinsic clearance) and Vu/F; the unbound concentration is
`Cu = central / vc` and the total concentration is `Cc = Cu / fu`, with a
linear (concentration-independent) unbound fraction. Absorption is first order
with a lag time. Gestational week `EGA` (the control streams' `WEEK`, coded 0
at the postpartum visit) raises CLu/F exponentially:

`CLu/F = theta * exp(coef * EGA)` (paper Eq 14).

Ritonavir CLu/F and Vu/F additionally scale with body weight (fixed exponents
0.75 and 1 about 70 kg). Interoccasion variability is carried over the four
study visits through the `OCC` column (1-4); `OCC = 0` gives the
occasion-free typical value.

# Source trace

  "fu", "0.0258", "0.149", "Table 2 (2.58%, 14.9%)",

  "IIV fu (variance)", "0.002116", "0.0597", "Table 2 %CV squared; S5 Part III",

  "IOV CLu/F (variance)", "0.061009", "-", "Table 2 24.7 %CV",

  knitr::kable(caption = "Source of every structural element and parameter value in the two packaged models.")
```

The paper's %CV is `100 * sqrt(omega^2)`, not `sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`. This
is read off the ritonavir values the authors fixed into their interaction
control streams, which reproduce every ritonavir %CV and the correlation in
Table 2 exactly under that convention:

```{r cv-convention}
rtv_omega <- c(cl = 0.0073, fu = 0.0597, cov = -0.0199, iov_ka = 2.01, iov_fu = 0.0551, iov_f = 0.131)
cv_check <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("IIV CLu/F", "IIV fu", "IOV ka", "IOV fu", "IOV F", "r(CL, fu)"),
  `Table 2` = c(8.5, 24.4, 141.8, 23.5, 36.2, -0.95),
  `From S5 omegas` = c(
    100 * sqrt(rtv_omega[c("cl", "fu", "iov_ka", "iov_fu", "iov_f")]),
    rtv_omega[["cov"]] / sqrt(rtv_omega[["cl"]] * rtv_omega[["fu"]])
  )
)
# Each Table 2 entry is printed to 2-4 significant figures; the omegas to 3.
# The realised relative deviations are 0.02%-0.52%, while the competing
# sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1) reading would print the ka entry as 254%, not 141.8%.
stopifnot(with(cv_check, max(abs(`From S5 omegas` / `Table 2` - 1)) < 0.01))
knitr::kable(cv_check, digits = 3)
```

# Derived parameters in Table 2 and Table 3

Table 2 footnotes a-b define the total-drug parameters as `CL/F = fu * CLu/F`
and `V/F = fu * Vu/F`. Table 3 lists the post hoc median clearances at each
visit; because lopinavir IIV on CLu/F is only 2.7%, the typical value
`167 * exp(0.0148 * EGA)` should land on those medians (visit 1 is taken at 22
weeks, the gestational age the Discussion uses for it).

```{r derived}
p <- lapply(uis, function(u) {
  th <- u$theta
  list(cl = exp(th[["lcl"]]), vc = exp(th[["lvc"]]), fu = exp(th[["lfu"]]), coef = th[["e_ega_cl"]])
})
derived <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("LPV CL/F (L/h)", "LPV V/F (L)", "RTV CL/F per 70 kg (L/h)", "RTV V/F per 70 kg (L)"),
  Published = c(4.31, 88.5, 23.8, 232),
  Model = c(
    p$lopinavir$fu * p$lopinavir$cl, p$lopinavir$fu * p$lopinavir$vc,
    p$ritonavir$fu * p$ritonavir$cl, p$ritonavir$fu * p$ritonavir$vc
  )
)
# Products of two 3-significant-figure values against a third: rounding alone
# is worth up to ~0.4%.
stopifnot(with(derived, max(abs(Model / Published - 1)) < 0.01))
knitr::kable(derived, digits = 3, caption = "Table 2 footnotes a-b reproduced from the packaged parameters.")

visits <- tibble::tibble(
  visit = c("Visit 1 (20-24 weeks)", "Visit 2 (30 weeks)", "Visit 3 (32 weeks)", "Visit 4 (8 weeks postpartum)"),
  EGA = c(22, 30, 32, 0),
  OCC = 1:4,
  dose_lpv = c(400, 400, 500, 400),
  dose_rtv = c(100, 100, 125, 100)
)
tab3 <- visits |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Table 3 CLu/F median` = c(232, 261, 269, 167),
    `Typical CLu/F` = p$lopinavir$cl * exp(p$lopinavir$coef * EGA),
    `Table 3 CL/F median` = c(5.92, 6.69, 6.94, 4.28),
    `Typical CL/F` = p$lopinavir$fu * `Typical CLu/F`,
    `Increase vs postpartum (%)` = 100 * (exp(p$lopinavir$coef * EGA) - 1)
  )
# The typical value is not the post hoc median, but with 2.7% IIV on CLu/F
# and 4.6% on fu the realised differences are 0%-0.3% (CLu/F) and
# 0.3%-0.8% (CL/F). A wrong coefficient (e.g. 0.0184 for 0.0148) moves the
# 32-week row by 12%.
stopifnot(
  with(tab3, max(abs(`Typical CLu/F` / `Table 3 CLu/F median` - 1))) < 0.02,
  with(tab3, max(abs(`Typical CL/F` / `Table 3 CL/F median` - 1))) < 0.02
)
tab3 |>
  dplyr::select(-OCC, -dose_lpv, -dose_rtv) |>
  dplyr::rename("Visit" = visit) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Lopinavir clearance by visit: typical value against the Table 3 post hoc medians (L/h).")
```

The increases over postpartum (38%, 56% and 61%) are the ones the Results
report for 20-24, 30 and 32 weeks.

# Typical-value steady-state profiles and PKNCA

Each visit is simulated at steady state (20 doses every 12 h, at the visit's
dose) for a typical woman. Ritonavir is simulated at the cohort's median
screening weight, 87.4 kg.

```{r typical}
tau <- 12
n_doses <- 20
last_dose <- (n_doses - 1) * tau
obs_t <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.25), seq(2, 6, by = 0.1), seq(6, 12, by = 0.5))))

# Event table built as a plain data.frame, with cmt set to the ODE state and
# an explicit dvid on every observation row: these models declare two
# endpoints (1 = total Cc, 2 = unbound Cu, in the order of the residual-error
# lines), so an observation row must say which endpoint it belongs to.
make_ss_events <- function(dose, ids, EGA, OCC, WT) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(
      id = ids, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot",
      ii = tau, addl = n_doses - 1L, dvid = NA_integer_
    ),
    tidyr::crossing(id = ids, toff = obs_t) |>
      dplyr::transmute(
        id, time = last_dose + toff, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central",
        ii = NA_real_, addl = NA_integer_, dvid = 2L
      )
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(EGA = EGA, OCC = OCC, WT = WT) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(uis), function(drug) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(visits)), function(i) {
    v <- visits[i, ]
    dose <- if (drug == "lopinavir") v$dose_lpv else v$dose_rtv
    ev <- make_ss_events(dose, ids = 1L, EGA = v$EGA, OCC = v$OCC, WT = 87.4)
    s <- rxode2::rxSolve(uis[[drug]], ev, omega = NA, sigma = NA, returnType = "data.frame")
    s |>
      dplyr::mutate(drug = drug, visit = v$visit, dose = dose, toff = time - last_dose)
  }))
}))
```

```{r typical-plot, fig.height = 6}
typ |>
  dplyr::select(drug, visit, toff, Total = Cc, Unbound = Cu) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Total, Unbound), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  ggplot(aes(toff, conc * 1000, colour = visit)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(analyte ~ drug, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

PKNCA is run on the steady-state dosing interval, with `drug`, `analyte` and
`visit` as the grouping. At steady state `Dose / AUC0-tau` (`cl.last`) is the
apparent oral clearance, so the unbound stream returns CLu/F and the total
stream CL/F, which Table 3 reports as post hoc medians per visit.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- typ |>
  dplyr::select(drug, visit, dose, time = toff, Total = Cc, Unbound = Cu) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Total, Unbound), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "Cc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(stream = paste(drug, analyte, visit, sep = " | "), id = 1L) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(stream, time)
# The interval starts at the last dose, so the time-zero row is the
# steady-state trough; assert it is present.
stopifnot(
  sim_nca |> dplyr::group_by(stream) |> dplyr::summarise(h = any(time == 0), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::pull(h) |> all(),
  dplyr::n_distinct(sim_nca$stream) == 16L
)
dose_df <- sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(stream, id, dose) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(as.data.frame(sim_nca), Cc ~ time | stream + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(as.data.frame(dose_df), dose ~ time | stream + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = tau, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE, cl.last = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "tmax", "cav")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(PPORRES = ifelse(PPTESTCD == "tmax", PPORRES, PPORRES * 1000)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = stream, names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-stream, ~ signif(.x, 3)))
nca_wide |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Drug | analyte | visit" = stream,
    "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax,
    "Cmin (ng/mL)" = cmin,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "Cavg (ng/mL)" = cav
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steady-state NCA of the typical-value profiles.")
```

```{r nca-compare}
table3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~analyte, ~visit_i, ~cl.last,
  "lopinavir", "Unbound", 1, 232, "lopinavir", "Unbound", 2, 261,
  "lopinavir", "Unbound", 3, 269, "lopinavir", "Unbound", 4, 167,
  "lopinavir", "Total", 1, 5.92, "lopinavir", "Total", 2, 6.69,
  "lopinavir", "Total", 3, 6.94, "lopinavir", "Total", 4, 4.28,
  "ritonavir", "Unbound", 1, 273, "ritonavir", "Unbound", 2, 337,
  "ritonavir", "Unbound", 3, 357, "ritonavir", "Unbound", 4, 178,
  "ritonavir", "Total", 1, 38.2, "ritonavir", "Total", 2, 52.3,
  "ritonavir", "Total", 3, 58.5, "ritonavir", "Total", 4, 26.9
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(stream = paste(drug, analyte, visits$visit[visit_i], sep = " | ")) |>
  dplyr::select(stream, cl.last)

cmp <- suppressWarnings(nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = table3,
  by = "stream",
  params = "cl.last",
  units = c(cl.last = "L/h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
))
cmp[[1]] <- "Apparent oral clearance Dose/AUC0-12 (L/h)"
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Typical-value Dose/AUC0-12 against the Table 3 post hoc median clearances (median, not typical value). * marks a row differing by more than 20%.",
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r")
)

recovered <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cl.last") |>
  dplyr::select(stream, simulated = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(table3, by = "stream") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (simulated - cl.last) / cl.last)
lpv_rec <- dplyr::filter(recovered, grepl("^lopinavir", stream))
rtv_u_rec <- dplyr::filter(recovered, grepl("^ritonavir \\| Unbound", stream))
# Deterministic solves. Lopinavir: realised deviations 0%-0.8%, set by the gap
# between a typical value and a post hoc median under 2.7% / 4.6% IIV, plus
# trapezoidal error. Ritonavir unbound: the typical woman is the 87.4 kg
# screening median, while the Table 3 medians pool the individual weights and
# etas at each visit; realised deviations 2.7%-6.1%. Both bands still fail on
# a mis-transcribed clearance, coefficient or fu, each worth >= 12%.
stopifnot(
  nrow(lpv_rec) == 8L, max(abs(lpv_rec$pct)) < 2,
  nrow(rtv_u_rec) == 4L, max(abs(rtv_u_rec$pct)) < 10
)
```

The lopinavir rows agree with Table 3 within 1%, and the ritonavir unbound
rows within about 6%. The ritonavir
total-clearance medians differ more (up to about 13% at visit 3). Ritonavir
CLu/F and fu are strongly negatively correlated between subjects (r = -0.95)
and fu varies between occasions by 23.5%, so the median of the post hoc product
`fu * CLu/F` need not equal the product of the typical values.

```{r fu-identity}
# Cu / Cc is fu by construction; an exactness check on the encoding.
fu_check <- typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(drug) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ratio = max(abs(Cu / Cc / fu - 1)), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(max(fu_check$ratio) < 1e-10)
```

# Visual predictive check (Figure 3)

Two hundred virtual women per visit are simulated at steady state, each
observed over one dosing interval with her own interindividual and
interoccasion draws and residual error. Body weight (needed by ritonavir only)
is drawn log-normally about the 87.4 kg screening median and truncated to the
published 45.3-142.6 kg range.

```{r vpc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160301)
n_per_visit <- 200
set.seed(20160301)
wt_pool <- exp(rnorm(4 * n_per_visit, log(87.4), 0.28))
wt_pool <- pmin(pmax(wt_pool, 45.3), 142.6)

vpc_obs_t <- c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12)
vpc <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(uis), function(drug) {
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(visits)), function(i) {
    v <- visits[i, ]
    ids <- (i - 1L) * n_per_visit + seq_len(n_per_visit)
    dose <- if (drug == "lopinavir") v$dose_lpv else v$dose_rtv
    one <- function(dvid) {
      dplyr::bind_rows(
        data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", ii = tau, addl = n_doses - 1L, dvid = NA_integer_),
        tidyr::crossing(id = ids, toff = vpc_obs_t) |>
          dplyr::transmute(id, time = last_dose + toff, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", ii = NA_real_, addl = NA_integer_, dvid = dvid)
      )
    }
    # Total (dvid 1) and unbound (dvid 2) observation rows at the same times;
    # the dose rows are kept once.
    dplyr::bind_rows(one(1L), dplyr::filter(one(2L), evid == 0L)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(EGA = v$EGA, OCC = v$OCC, WT = wt_pool[id], visit = v$visit)
  })) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  rxode2::rxSolve(uis[[drug]], ev, keep = c("visit", "dvid"), returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::mutate(drug = drug)
}))

vpc_sum <- vpc |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    toff = time - last_dose,
    analyte = ifelse(dvid == 1L, "Total", "Unbound")
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(drug, analyte, visit, toff) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05) * 1000,
    p50 = quantile(sim, 0.50) * 1000,
    p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95) * 1000,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r vpc-plot, fig.height = 9, fig.cap = "Replicates the prediction percentiles of Figure 3 of Chen 2016 (rows: unbound LPV, total LPV, unbound RTV, total RTV; columns: visits 1-4). Lines: simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles."}
vpc_sum |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    row = factor(paste(analyte, drug), levels = c("Unbound lopinavir", "Total lopinavir", "Unbound ritonavir", "Total ritonavir")),
    visit = sub(" \\(.*$", "", visit)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(toff)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_grid(row ~ visit, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (hr)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

The simulated medians lie in the same ranges as the Figure 3 prediction
medians: unbound lopinavir of about 100-200 ng/mL in pregnancy and 170-240
ng/mL postpartum, total lopinavir of about 4,000-9,000 ng/mL, unbound ritonavir
of about 10-60 ng/mL and total ritonavir of about 80-400 ng/mL, with the
highest concentrations of both drugs at the postpartum visit. Figure 3 is
compared visually only; no curve was digitised from it.

# Inhibitory quotients (Table 4, Supplementary Tables S7 and S8)

The authors simulated 1,000 subjects at 32 weeks of gestation and postpartum
under 400/100, 500/125 and 600/150 mg twice daily, took the unbound LPV trough
12 h after a steady-state dose, and computed the inhibitory quotient
`IQ = Cu,trough / IC50` with the wild-type IC50 of 0.69 ng/mL and IC50s raised
4-, 10-, 20- and 40-fold. IQ > 15 counts as effective and IQ < 4 as
ineffective. Here 200 subjects are simulated per arm (six arms). The IQs are
summarised on the simulated observation (`sim`, which carries the proportional
residual error) rather than on the individual prediction: both reproduce the
published means, but only the former reproduces the published SDs, so the
authors' IQs evidently included residual error.

```{r iq}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160302)
n_arm <- 200
arms <- tidyr::crossing(dose = c(400, 500, 600), EGA = c(32, 0)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(arm = dplyr::row_number())
iq_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1L) * n_arm + seq_len(n_arm)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, amt = arms$dose[i], evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", ii = tau, addl = n_doses - 1L, dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = ids, time = last_dose + tau, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", ii = NA_real_, addl = NA_integer_, dvid = 2L)
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(EGA = arms$EGA[i], OCC = 1L, arm = i)
})) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
iq_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(uis$lopinavir, iq_ev, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::select(id, arm, sim) |>
  dplyr::left_join(arms, by = "arm")

ic50_wt <- 0.69 # ng/mL, wild-type protein-free IC50 (Methods 'Virologic parameters')
iq_tab <- iq_sim |>
  tidyr::crossing(fold = c(1, 4, 10, 20, 40)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(IQ = sim * 1000 / (ic50_wt * fold)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose, EGA, fold) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_sim = mean(IQ), sd_sim = sd(IQ),
    lt4_sim = 100 * mean(IQ < 4), gt15_sim = 100 * mean(IQ > 15),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Supplementary Tables S7 (third trimester) and S8 (postpartum); Table 4 repeats
# the mean, SD and %IQ > 15 columns.
published_iq <- tibble::tribble(

iq_cmp <- dplyr::inner_join(iq_tab, published_iq, by = c("dose", "EGA", "fold"))
stopifnot(nrow(iq_cmp) == 30L)

wt_rows <- dplyr::filter(iq_cmp, fold == 1)
# The arm mean is the centre of 200 draws with a ~40% CV, so its Monte Carlo
# SE is about 3%; the published means carry their own 1,000-subject noise.
# A 10% band is >3 SE wide yet fails on a mis-transcribed clearance,
# coefficient or volume, each of which shifts the trough by 12% or more.
stopifnot(max(abs(wt_rows$mean_sim / wt_rows$mean_pub - 1)) < 0.10)

```{r iq-table}
iq_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    State = ifelse(EGA == 32, "32 weeks", "Postpartum"),
    Regimen = paste0(dose, "/", dose / 4, " mg BID"),
    IC50 = ifelse(fold == 1, "wild type", paste0(fold, "-fold")),
    `IQ mean +/- SD (sim)` = sprintf("%.1f +/- %.1f", mean_sim, sd_sim),
    `IQ mean +/- SD (paper)` = sprintf("%.1f +/- %.1f", mean_pub, sd_pub),
    `%IQ < 4 sim / paper` = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", lt4_sim, lt4_pub),
    `%IQ > 15 sim / paper` = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", gt15_sim, gt15_pub)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(EGA), dose, fold) |>
  dplyr::select(State, Regimen, IC50, dplyr::starts_with("IQ mean"), dplyr::starts_with("%IQ")) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Table 4 and Supplementary Tables S7-S8 of Chen 2016 (200 simulated subjects per arm here, 1,000 in the paper).")
```

The simulated means, SDs and effectiveness fractions follow the published ones
closely across all thirty cells. The paper's conclusion is reproduced: with up
to a 4-fold rise in IC50 more than 90% of women at 32 weeks reach an effective
IQ on the standard 400/100 mg dose, a 10-fold rise leaves fewer than half
effective at that dose, and with a 40-fold rise 90% or more of women fail to
reach an effective IQ on every regimen, in pregnancy and postpartum.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Unbound-side parameterisation.** `cl` and `vc` are the apparent *unbound*
  parameters CLu/F and Vu/F, as in the authors' control streams. The total-drug
  CL/F and V/F of Table 2 are the products with `fu` and are reproduced above.

- **%CV convention.** Variances are `(CV/100)^2`, confirmed against the
  ritonavir omegas the authors fixed into their interaction control streams
  (see the source-trace section). The ritonavir IIV block and IOV variances are
  taken from those control streams (0.0073, -0.0199, 0.0597; 2.01, 0.0551,
  0.131), which carry one more significant figure than Table 2. The lopinavir
  omegas are not printed in any control stream and come from Table 2.

- **Residual errors are independent across the two streams.** Both control
  streams estimate the correlation between the total and unbound residual
  errors with `$SIGMA BLOCK(2)` (r = 0.614 for LPV, 0.611 for RTV, Table 2).
  nlmixr2 has no cross-endpoint residual correlation, so `propSd` and
  `propSd_Cu` are independent here. Marginal residual variability is correct;
  the joint spread of a paired total/unbound simulated sample is not.

- **Interaction models not packaged.** The joint LPV-RTV models of
  Supplementary Material S4-S5 (RTV inhibition of LPV clearance by unbound RTV
  AUC or concentration) did not improve the fit significantly and were not
  adopted by the authors. Their LPV parameters other than CLu/F, the
  interaction coefficient and the gestational coefficient are not reported, so
  they could not be packaged in any case.

- **A `non-mu referenced` note is expected on model load.** The occasion
  multiplexers (`oc1 * etaiov_ka_1 + ...`) place the interoccasion etas
  outside a mu-referenced position, so rxode2 emits "some etas defaulted to
  non-mu referenced". This affects estimation efficiency, not simulation, and
  is shared by every IOV-multiplexing model in the library.

- **Gestational age of visit 1.** Visit 1 spanned 20-24 weeks; 22 weeks is used
  here, the value the Discussion assigns to it when quoting the 38% increase.

- **Occasion.** All simulations here use a single occasion per subject
  (`OCC` = the visit number in the VPC, `OCC = 1` for the IQ arms), so each
  virtual woman draws one set of occasion effects per simulated visit.

- **Body weight distribution.** Only the median (87.4 kg) and range
  (45.3-142.6 kg) of screening weight are published. The VPC cohort draws
  weight log-normally (log-SD 0.28, an assumption) about that median, truncated
  to that range. Weight enters only the ritonavir model, and no quantitative
  check above depends on the weight distribution.

- **No published NCA.** The paper's own NCA (Supplementary Material S3) is
  shown only graphically as unbound AUC fractions. The PKNCA comparison above
  therefore uses the Table 3 post hoc median clearances as the reference.
